origin: T33 hand-off (Ian team research, 2026-10-24); re-verified by T38

source.title: Twenty years of misdiagnosis of X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy: a case report.

accessException.reason: Publisher copyright ("AJTR Copyright © 2025"); not in the PMC open-access set and no Creative Commons licence. Free to read on PMC only.
accessException.decision: Kept in the held-out split: the held-out set is defined as the 10 T33 cases and has already been scored once, so replacing the case would rewrite the evaluation history. Flagged as an exception to the open-access requirement.
accessException.use: Only short quotes (at most 30 words) for verification and a paraphrased note; article text is not stored in the repository or redistributed.

confirmation.summary: Raised plasma VLCFA ratios and a novel hemizygous ABCD1 c.356dupC found by Sanger sequencing.
evidence: VLCFA analysis indicated elevated plasma ratios of C24/C22 (1.46; reference range: 0.64-0.98) and C26/C22
Sanger sequencing detected a novel potentially pathogenic hemizygous mutation (Figure 2) at exon 1 (c.356dupC) in the ABCD1 gene

note.text: My legs have grown stiffer and weaker over many years. At first walking only felt awkward, but the problem gradually became so severe that I needed a wheelchair. Sometimes my legs felt numb, and I started walking with my feet far apart to keep my balance. Other people noticed that some of my words were harder to understand. I've also had muscle cramps, changes in my mood and problems controlling when I go to the bathroom.
note.author: T33 hand-off (assistant-written from the article; not the patient's words)

phenotypes.label: Muscle weakness
phenotypes.evidence: initially manifested as rigidity and weakness in both legs since 1998
phenotypes.notePhrase: My legs have grown stiffer and weaker

phenotypes.label: Lower limb spasticity
phenotypes.evidence: a persistent increase in cogwheel muscle tone in both lower limbs

phenotypes.label: Gait disturbance
phenotypes.evidence: a 20-year history of progressively worsening gait disturbances

phenotypes.label: Broad-based gait
phenotypes.evidence: spastic paraparesis accompanied by a wide-based spastic gait
phenotypes.notePhrase: walking with my feet far apart

phenotypes.label: Hypoesthesia
phenotypes.evidence: Numbness in the lower limbs was reported by the patient in 2003

phenotypes.label: Dysarthria
phenotypes.evidence: Neurological examination revealed impaired cognitive function, mild dysarthria, and spastic paraparesis
phenotypes.notePhrase: some of my words were harder to understand

phenotypes.label: Muscle spasm
phenotypes.evidence: Additional manifestations included asynodia, muscle cramps, and psychiatric conditions
phenotypes.comment: HPO lists 'muscle cramps' as a synonym of Muscle spasm.

phenotypes.label: Hyperreflexia
phenotypes.evidence: Deep tendon reflexes were diffusely brisk, with a bilateral Achilles clonus and a positive Babinski sign
phenotypes.comment: Examination finding; not in the note.

uncertainty: The article is not open-access licensed (see source.accessException), and NCBI does not allow automated full-text download. Quotes were checked by reading the public PMC page on 2026-10-24 and cannot be re-checked by verify-sources.

The note mentions mood changes and bathroom control; the article reports anxiety, depression, apathy and sphincter dysfunction, but these are not coded here because the note's wording is too general to pick one HPO term.
